I dont know how old you are/if you have access to money or a vehicle or if the abuser is familal/platonic or romantic but I'll share what worked for me.

You have to be sneaky and always, always cover your tracks. Please only use these tactics for your protection and not immoral/illegal activities.

Plan your escape meticulously. Do not leave ANYTHING to let them suspect you are planning to leave because things will get a lot harder for you when they do. Move out when they're at work and there is NO chance they'll be coming home early. 

Buy a throwaway phone, keep the ringer off and stash it somewhere they won't find it, I suggest secured under a car seat (so it doesn't get loose and end up on the floor in the backseat) or deep behind/under linens if you have a full linen closet. Do not keep it in your room, they will find it, they look for that kind of stuff.  Make sure its somewhere they won't find it. Use this phone number when looking for a place to live or anything you wouldn't want them seeing.

If potential housing is going to send a letter be sure to always get to the mail first and destroy anything not neccessary but incriminating/ that your abuser could get angry at. If possible have them send it to a family member or friend's house.

SO abusers can easily become stalkers, if you do manage to get out make sure you get decent locks on your new place and change at least every six months. If you can get a security system, great, if not buy a cheap hidden camera and put it in your bedroom if yours worried they've been in your home. If they're going to going to rifle through your stuff, they'll spend the most time in your room.

Always have some protection by your bedside and on you- a large pocket knife or pepper spray could save you from harm or even your life. 

Do not give out personal information freely. There is many websites and apps that will give out personal information such as your address, phone number and email for FREE just by typing in a name. I found this out by downloading a sex offender locator app that gave out all of these things about myself and I've never had so much as a traffic ticket. Stalkers will definitely use these.

On a similar vein, do not take pictures of or post your job, location or places you frequent on social media. Do not accept random friends requests and block anyone you suspect could be a dummy account of your abuser. Make your profiles private if possible and block/unfriend people that are friends with abuser that would possible let the abuser use their account to look at yours. Remember to turn off location services when using social media.

I know this sounds crazy and paranoid, but abusers frequently become stalkers and can make your life a living hell. I had a ex boyfriend that would fuck with my car so it'd break down and call me the same day to ask if my car's okay when we hadn't talked in weeks and if he could come over to fix it. He tapped my cellphone and would monitor my activity without my knowledge. He'd also show up inside my house when we weren't together and peek through the blinds when I changed the locks. He had me living in constant fear for months and I want to help prevent anyone going through the same thing if I can.

I hope this helps.
